title: Opportunistic covered calls beat writing calls every month
summary: The speaker tracks covered-call ETFs against their benchmarks. One fund with a current-income goal that writes calls only opportunistically, for example near resistance, outperformed almost all funds that sell calls systematically. A covered-call program needs a rule for when to stop.

steps.caption: A dividend stock path over one month. It stalls near resistance below $105. The fund holds the shares all the time.
The fund sells calls only at chosen moments, for example when the price hits resistance.
The $105 call caps the gain only while it is open.
The call expires worthless. With calls off after expiry, the shares would keep all upside if the price later breaks out.
The speaker found such an opportunistic fund beat almost all systematic covered-call funds.

takeaways: Compare covered-call funds with their underlying benchmark, not only with their yield.
The fund the speaker found sells calls opportunistically, such as near resistance, and suspends them at other times.
That fund outperformed almost all the funds that write calls systematically.
caveats: The speaker names the fund only in the caption (DIVO); performance claims are not verified here.
The transcript promotes the speaker's upcoming Discord.
